title: Graph-aware tool hooks + master-index autoupdate + octopus auto-invoke repair
rationale: Three connected under-utilization gaps in PRISM's own AI/awareness infrastructure. (1) Only the Read tool consults the system-viz master graph; Grep/Write/Bash do not, and key derivation is a crude basename. (2) system-graph.json (412MB) is 9.5h stale -- its post-commit autoupdate spawns in background with exit code ignored and fails silently; the graph exceeds master-index-search-lib's 200MB load cap so search depends entirely on the 109MB sidecar, which when stale degrades search fleet-wide to a 20K-node fallback. (3) Octopus 5-LLM consensus is fully built (5 client engines, MultiModelConsensusEngine, 4 hooks) but consensus-model-performance.json is frozen at 2026-05-05 n=1 ema=0 -- it has never meaningfully run; a 72-entry consensus-queue.jsonl is not draining. Goal: fill all gaps, build and wire everything.
intent: do everything in logical ROI order; all gaps filled, all tasks completed and wired

close_out_log.finding: The graph autoupdate stalls from a cluster of structural flaws. (1) Crashed regen runs leave stale lock files: .system-viz-on-commit.pid AND .system-graph-write.pid both held pid 24784, a dead process. (2) Windows PID-reuse phantom: process.kill(pid,0) returns 'alive' when an unrelated process inherits a recycled pid number, so a stale lock reads as live and every run skips forever. (3) Silent skip: the post-commit hook runs `node ... >/dev/null 2>&1 &` — a skip exits 0 and the hook discards it, so 9.5h of staleness was invisible. (4) No completion sentinel. (5) SECOND finding: a backgrounded regen-viz run orphaned (parent shell exited) ran all ~40 augmentation generators then died before the merge stage — likely OOM (host runs 80-96% memory pressure) or fleet-reaper reap of the orphan; the graph was never written.

Fix shipped: (a) scripts/lib/system-graph-write-lock.mjs — TTL backstop (DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_MS 30min, knob PRISM_SYSTEM_GRAPH_WRITE_LOCK_TTL_MS): decideAcquire/decideActive reclaim any lock whose file mtime exceeds the TTL regardless of the pid probe, defeating the phantom; additive (lockAgeMs=null when mtime unavailable preserves all pre-existing fake-fs tests). 35/35 tests (24 original + 11 new TTL). (b) scripts/system-viz-on-commit.mjs — pidFileGuard given the same mtime-TTL backstop; writeRegenSentinel stamps .last-successful-regen.json on every successful chain so staleness is observable despite the hook discarding stdout. NOT YET DONE in B2: post-commit hook fail-loud routing (managed-marker file — deferred to B4); inline pidFileGuard could be further DRYed against the shared lib. Orphan-OOM mitigation is a B4 concern (backstop).

regen-viz.mjs ALREADY chained build-graph-index.mjs (the sidecar builder) at its lines 346-352 — but system-viz-on-commit.mjs (the git post-commit chain, the DOMINANT graph writer, fires every commit) did NOT. So every post-commit regen advanced system-graph.json and left system-graph-index.json stale; loadGraph's staleness gate (sidecar.sourceMtimeMs >= graph.mtimeMs) then rejected the stale sidecar and master-index search degraded fleet-wide to the 20K-node architecture-graph fallback. Observed: sidecar 2 days stale (2026-05-20) behind a fresh 431MB graph (2026-05-22 16:23). Fix: (a) rebuilt the sidecar immediately — 258,874 nodes / 111.9MB / 16.5s — un-degrading fleet search now; (b) added rebuildMasterIndexSidecar(node,runFn), an exported dependency-injected helper that spawns build-graph-index.mjs with an explicit raised V8 heap, into system-viz-on-commit.mjs main() after the refresh chain succeeds (graph fresh, shared write-lock still held), threading a sidecarOk boolean into the .last-successful-regen.json sentinel and logging fail-loud on failure. Non-fatal: a sidecar miss degrades search to the legacy path, never the graph. 4 new tests (2 unit DI + 2 real-subprocess E2E: build->sidecar->runMasterIndexSearch hit, and the stale-sidecar fail-loud rejection); 20/20 green. 2-of-2 scrutiny PASS, 0 P0/P1.

Two halves, both shipped. (1) FAIL-LOUD: the post-commit hook discards stderr (>/dev/null 2>&1), so a graceful chain failure left no trace — only success was observable (B2's sentinel). Added a script-managed companion marker .last-regen-failure.json: system-viz-on-commit.mjs's run() now captures the failed stage / exit code / signal / stderr-tail into a module-level lastRunFailure; main()'s if(!ok) block writes it via the new exported writeRegenFailure() before process.exit(1). Atomic, structured, captures the stderr, works in ALL clones immediately (chose this over editing the post-commit redirect — the installer skips when the marker block exists so a redirect change would only help future clones). Success + failure markers never delete each other; B5 will compare their ts. (2) AUTOUPDATE BACKSTOP: new .claude/hooks/stop-graph-staleness-backstop.mjs (T3 Stop hook). On every chat Stop it stats the graph; if age > PRISM_GRAPH_STALENESS_BACKSTOP_HRS (default 3) AND a fleet-shared throttle marker .graph-backstop-spawn.json was not touched in PRISM_GRAPH_STALENESS_BACKSTOP_THROTTLE_MIN (default 30) min, it detached-spawns scripts/system-viz-on-commit.mjs and emits {continue:true, systemMessage:'graph stale Xh — triggered background regen'}. Pure decideBackstop({graphMtimeMs,lastSpawnMs,nowMs,thresholdMs,throttleMs}) core is fully tested (11 cases — fresh, threshold-boundary, stale, throttled, missing graph, clock-skew, NaN). Throttle is best-effort dedup (last-write-wins); the on-commit pid guard + shared graph-write lock are the hard mutex (worst case: N detached spawns of which N-1 self-skip immediately). With 26 chats the graph cannot stay stale unnoticed. Wired at Stop[0].hooks[52] in C:/Users/wompu/.claude/settings.json (c-to-h-mirror replicated to H:/.claude/settings.json). Smoke-tested live: returns SILENCE on the fresh production graph. Tests: 1 new on-commit (writeRegenFailure schema pin for B5) + 14 backstop (11 pure + 3 hermetic subprocess E2E with mkdtemp fixtures — none can spawn a real regen). 21/21 + 14/14 green. 2-of-2 scrutiny PASS, 0 P0; Arm A flagged 4 P1s — all are convention misunderstandings (cross-tree-collision template uses the same hard-coded H:/prism ROOT; the 30-100-line guideline is for .sh hooks not .mjs; the throttle race is documented and the pid guard is the documented hard mutex; knob docs live in the hook header per convention).

New T2 SessionStart hook .claude/hooks/sessionstart-graph-staleness-inject.mjs reads the four B2/B3/B4 artifacts (graph + sidecar mtimes + .last-successful-regen.json + .last-regen-failure.json) and emits ONE concise advisory in priority order: (1) last regen FAILED (failure ts > sentinel ts) — surfaces stage / exit / stderr tail; (2) graph missing; (3) graph older than PRISM_GRAPH_STALENESS_INJECT_HRS (default 6h — lenient vs B4's 3h spawn threshold so a backstop-spawned fresh regen does not re-surface the warning); (4) sidecar missing OR built from an older graph (loadGraph staleness gate rejects → search degrades to the architecture fallback); else silent. Pure decideStalenessAdvisory({graphMtimeMs,sidecarMtimeMs,sentinelTs,failureTs,failure,nowMs,staleHrs}) is the testable core — 12 cases (every branch + boundaries + clock skew + adversarial NaN + missing-stage failure object). Plus 3 subprocess E2E (silence on fresh, sidecar-stale advisory rendered as SessionStart additionalContext markdown, disable knob). 15/15 green. Wired at SessionStart[0].hooks tail in C:/Users/wompu/.claude/settings.json (c-to-h-mirror replicated). Smoke-tested live: SILENCE on fresh production graph + freshly-rebuilt sidecar. 2-of-2 scrutiny PASS, 0 P0; both reviewers flagged the strict-`>` staleness boundary as documented-in-tests-but-not-in-source — fixed with an in-line comment pinning the contract. Track B (B1-B5) is now complete — graph freshness + sidecar guarantee + autoupdate backstop + fail-loud + staleness visibility all shipped, scrutinized, and live in the fleet.

New pure lib scripts/lib/graph-key-derive.mjs — the shared key-derivation core for the 4 PreToolUse graph-injection hooks (A2-A5). deriveGraphKeys({input,tool,maxKeys}) with per-tool strategies: read/write → basename stem, dash+underscore split, tokenize; grep → tokenize the pattern directly (tokenize already strips ALL regex metachars via [^\p{L}\p{N}_\s] + drops STOPWORDS + dedups + caps — no manual metachar stripping needed); bash → NARROW, only fires on file-search verbs (grep/rg/find/cat/head/tail/ls), walks past env-var prefixes + the rtk wrapper, returns [] for git/npm/node/cargo/etc. Reuses tokenize from master-index-search-lib.mjs so the STOPWORDS set + MIN_TOKEN_LEN=3 + length caps are a single source of truth (the 'high-ROI filter' the plan called for — STOPWORDS already drops generic noise like 'system'/'engine'/'the'). 27 tests covering every tool branch + edge cases (empty/null/non-string input, NaN/0/negative maxKeys, all-metachar pattern, all-stopword pattern, oversize DoS, multi-command bash, find -name globs). 27/27 green. 2-of-2 scrutiny PASS, 0 P0/P1 (Arm B's one P1 — untested multi-command/find-name bash paths — closed with 2 added tests before commit). Three connected units shipped in one disciplined hook: .claude/hooks/auto-consensus-sync-bash.mjs — PreToolUse:Bash sync octopus trigger gated by an irreversibility-class classifier. C2 (sync auto-invoke at decision points) + C3 (surface consensus result in-context) + C4 (stakes-gated triggering) are subsumed by the same hook because the classifier IS the stakes gate, the sync ask() IS the decision-point trigger, and the verdict-as-permissionDecisionReason IS the in-context surface. CLASSIFIER (pure, 5 irreversibility classes — each tested): git-force-push (-f / --force / --force-with-lease), git-hard-reset (--hard), git-branch-force-delete (-D / --delete-force), rm-recursive-force (-rf / -fr / --recursive --force, deliberately NOT -f alone so `rm -f .git/index.lock` stays a no-op), git-clean-force (-f without -n dry-run). Walks past env-var prefixes (FOO=bar VERB) + the rtk wrapper; multi-command chains classify on the FIRST sub-command (conservative under-trigger — zero false positives). SAFETY INVARIANT: a classified destructive command can ONLY reach permissionDecision='allow' via a real consensus rec='accept'. Every other branch (no-env default, disable-knob, opt-in + engine-missing / timeout / throw / escalate / review / unknown rec, classifier-throw) → permissionDecision='ask'. DEFAULT BEHAVIOR (no env): match → ASK with class-naming reason (zero-cost, predictable latency). OPT-IN (PRISM_AUTO_CONSENSUS_SYNC_BASH=1): match → spawn MultiModelConsensusEngine.ask() with a 10s Promise.race timeout → translate rec to ask|allow. PRISM_AUTO_CONSENSUS_SYNC_DISABLE=1 only SUPPRESSES the LLM call on match; the ASK still fires (closes Arm A P0 from first-pass scrutiny where the disable knob short-circuited to silent allow before classification). PRISM_AUTO_CONSENSUS_SYNC_ENGINE_PATH overrides the engine candidates list (single path) — used by tests to deterministically force engine-unreachable OR inject a stub engine. clearTimeout in finally (closes Arm A P1 timer leak). 26 tests: 9 classifier (5 classes × ≥2 variants + null/non-destructive/env-prefix/rtk/multi-cmd-chain), 5 renderVerdict pure (icon-by-rec hard-asserted), 12 E2E (disable+non-match silent-allow, disable+MATCH still-asks safety lock, missing command, non-Bash, non-destructive, default-ask, opt-in+engine-unreachable hard-assert ask, stub-engine accept→allow, stub-engine escalate→ask, stub-engine throw→ask, stub-engine hang→timeout→ask). 26/26 green. 2-of-2 scrutiny PASS after one retry — both reviewers FAILED first pass (Arm A on safety-invariant breach via disable knob; Arm B on tautological ask||allow assertion), both PASSED retry after the classify-first reorder + deterministic engine-path env knob + stub-engine pattern. Wired in C:/Users/wompu/.claude/settings.json PreToolUse:Bash with 15000ms timeout (c-to-h-mirror replicated). Octopus is now LIVE on the irreversibility class: every rm -rf / git push --force / git reset --hard / git branch -D / git clean -f triggers operator visibility, and (when opt-in is set) actual 5-LLM consensus.

Both WIRE-EXEMPT stub engines replaced with real implementations. The stubs threw on every call; MultiModelConsensusEngine.ts wrapped both call sites in try/catch (lines 199 + 222-227) and fell back to a degraded path — confirmed in C1's audit (agreement_score=0, voters=null on every drained run). REAL IMPLEMENTATIONS: (1) PRISMContextInjectorEngine.ts — lazy-imports scripts/lib/master-index-search-lib.mjs, tokenizes the consensus prompt, runs BM25 over PRISM's 258K-node master graph, composes a markdown '### Relevant PRISM context' blob from the top hits (layer/status/label/info), capped at modelBudget chars (default 2000, clamped [200, 8000]). Returns the contract-correct { text, facts, budget, prompt } shape (fixing the old stub's prompt/facts/budget mismatch with the consumer at line 200 which uses ctx.text). Fail-open on every path. (2) ConsensusModelPerformanceEngine.ts — loadState(path?) reads a JSON state file at the given path with shape { schemaVersion, vendors: { [vendor]: { [taskType]: {ema, n, lastUpdate} } } }; missing file / invalid JSON / wrong shape → empty state (cold-start), NEVER throws. recommendVendors(state, taskType, available, {floor}) returns the contract-correct { ranked: RankedVendor[], rationale } shape (consumer at line 224 uses rec.ranked.map(r=>r.vendor) — old stub's { vendors:string[] } shape was the 'rec.ranked' tsc error). 3-branch keep-set ladder: cold-start (all-zero ema → keep ALL); signal mode (nonZero >= floor → keep nonZero); partial signal (nonZero < floor → pad scored.slice(0,floor)). Hard floor clamped to available.length so consensus can NEVER collapse below floor. Bonus: new pure recordOutcome(state, vendor, taskType, reward, alpha=0.2) with canonical EMA update (newEma = prev.ema + alpha * (clampedReward - prev.ema)), reward clamped to [0,1], alpha clamped to (0,1] — caller persists. TSC: previously-reported '3 tsc errors in MultiModelConsensusEngine.ts' are now CLEAN — the consumer call sites compile against the real engines without complaint. TESTS: 32/32 vitest tests in mcp-server/src/__tests__/ConsensusEngines.test.ts covering composeContext (pure: 6 cases incl. byte-truncation + head-anchor + defensive null/non-object hits), buildContext (5 cases incl. clamp-up MIN_BUDGET + lib-integration regression guard with hard XOR populated-vs-fail-open assert + R12 fail-loud anti-regression on a healthy graph), loadState (4 cases incl. missing-file / invalid-JSON / 5 wrong-shape variants / valid parse), recommendVendors (8 cases covering all 3 keep-set branches + task-typed scoring divergence + NaN ema + degenerate floor + non-array available), recordOutcome (5 cases incl. EMA math hard-asserted at 0.6 = 0.5 + 0.2*(1.0-0.5), reward-clamp [0,1], semantic-immutability assertions on rejection paths, degenerate alpha normalization). 2-of-2 scrutiny PASS — Arm A 0 P0/P1; Arm B 4 P1s all closed in the same session (P1-A semantic-immutability instead of reference-equality; P1-B head-anchor on truncation test; P1-C real-graph hard-assert with R12 fail-loud; P1-D MIN_BUDGET clamp-up branch). Octopus consensus is no longer running degraded — context injection + perf-weighted voter selection are now live and load-bearing.

Queue went 54 → 50 with 4 entries persisted to consensus-queue-processed.jsonl, each with {drain_ok:true, drain_error:null, has_recommendation:true}.
